name: Marco Girolamo Vida
credit: Portrait of Marco Girolamo Vida, engraving (c. 1597-1599), Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-1909-4363 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Marco Girolamo Vida (c. 1485-1566) was born in Cremona and became one of the leading Latin poets of the Italian Renaissance. He wrote in the classical manner, with Virgil as his model, and worked as a churchman: he was made bishop of Alba in 1532 and held the see until his death in 1566.

He is best known for the Christias, a Latin epic in six books on the Passion of Christ, which he wrote at the request of Pope Leo X and which was printed at Cremona in 1535. He also wrote De arte poetica (1527), a poem on the craft of poetry, and a Latin poem on the game of chess.
